blocks.text: Pensacola, United States — The southeastern United States faced flooding and tornado risks on Saturday as Isaias, weakened from a hurricane to a post-tropical cyclone, advanced northward from its landfall on Florida’s Gulf Coast. More than 600,000 US customers were without electricity Saturday afternoon along the storm’s path through Florida, Alabama and Georgia, according to the PowerOutage.com tracker. Isaias roared ashore late Friday as a Category 2 hurricane near the resort community of Destin, Florida, packing sustained winds of 105 miles (165 kilometers) per hour, before weakening overnight, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said.
